headline: Underwriting strength and lower catastrophes lift profit
summary_short: Travelers' Q2 FY2026 net income rose 46% y/y to $2.208 billion ($10.26 diluted EPS), with the combined ratio improving 6.7 points to 83.6% on lower catastrophe losses and higher favorable prior-year reserve development.
summary_long: Core income of $2.160 billion (+44% y/y) benefited from lower catastrophe losses ($518M vs $927M), higher net favorable prior-year reserve development ($578M vs $315M), a 14% increase in net investment income to $883 million after-tax, and a stronger underlying underwriting gain. Net written premiums were roughly flat at $11.529 billion; excluding the divested Canadian book, they grew 2%. All three segments held or improved their underlying combined ratios. The company returned $1.577 billion of capital, including $1.311 billion of buybacks, and book value per share rose 21% y/y to $158.81. Management guided the full-year 2026 underwriting expense ratio to approximately 28.5%.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the increase to higher core income and higher net realized investment gains ($48M after-tax vs $5M in the prior-year quarter).
Driven by lower catastrophe losses, higher net favorable prior-year reserve development, higher net investment income, and a higher underlying underwriting gain, per the release.
Improvement attributed to lower catastrophe losses (3.6 pts), higher favorable prior-year reserve development (2.5 pts), and a better underlying combined ratio (0.6 pts).
Roughly flat y/y as reported; ex-Canada (divested in Q1 2026) premiums grew 2%, with Bond & Specialty (+14%) and Business Insurance (+3%) offsetting an 8% decline in Personal Insurance.
CEO Schnitzer cited "very strong underwriting performance across all three segments" and a "terrific result" from the investment portfolio as the quarter's overall drivers.
